sections.content:
Now I see the pattern more clearly. The green block that appeared is at the same position as one of the original green blocks - specifically at boundary `[[13, 50], [13, 52], [14, 53], [16, 53], [17, 52], [17, 50], [16, 49], [14, 49]]` which was the rightmost green block in the middle row (rows 13-17, col 50-52).
So the mechanic seems to be:
1. ACTION7 respawns/replaces one green block at a time (cycling through the original positions)
2. MOUSE collects green blocks
3. The sky blue region has grown to 2014 pixels (was 1529 before collecting all 7)
Wait, actually let me reconsider. Maybe ACTION7 is like a "place" action that puts a green block at a specific location. The game might be about placing green blocks in the right positions to form a pattern or fill a shape.
Looking at the original 7 green block positions:
- Top row: cols 14-16, 20-22, 26-28 (rows 1-5)
- Middle row: cols 32-34, 38-40, 44-46, 50-52 (rows 13-17)
The new green block is at cols 50-52, rows 13-17 - the rightmost middle position.
Maybe the game is about filling the sky blue area with green blocks? Or maybe ACTION7 places green blocks one at a time in a cycle, and we need to collect them at the right time?
Let me think about this differently. The sky blue region now has 2014 pixels. Originally there were 2 sky blue regions (276 and 1529 pixels). After collecting all 7 green blocks, the sky blue region became one connected region of 2014 pixels. The green blocks that were collected became sky blue.
Now ACTION7 placed a new green block at the rightmost middle position. Maybe the goal is to:
1. Use ACTION7 to place green blocks in specific positions
2. Use MOUSE to collect them
3. Repeat until some condition is met
Or maybe the goal is simpler - just collect all green blocks that exist, and ACTION7 is used to spawn more. Let me try collecting this green block and see if more appear.
